name: Ptolemais
desc: An ancient city founded by the Egyptian Ptolemies, rich in large Hellenistic palaces.

name: Taucheira (Tocra)
desc: One of the five ancient cities of Cyrenaica, surrounded by strong Byzantine walls.

name: Ghadames Old Town
desc: Known as the pearl of the desert, the city is distinguished by its traditional mud-brick architecture and covered alleys.

name: Arch of Marcus Aurelius
desc: A Roman triumphal arch in Tripoli, the only surviving Roman monument in the city.

name: Red Castle (Assaraya al-Hamra)
desc: A massive fortress in Tripoli with a rich history spanning Ottoman and Spanish periods.

name: Tadrart Acacus
desc: A desert area containing prehistoric rock art that shows environmental and lifestyle changes.

name: Germa (Garama)
desc: The ancient capital of the Garamantes, a people who controlled the Saharan trade routes in antiquity.

name: Sanctuary of Slonta
desc: A mysterious pre-Islamic temple featuring unique, grotesque sculptures carved into the rock.

name: Villa Silin
desc: A luxurious Roman coastal villa near Leptis Magna featuring well-preserved mosaics and frescoes.

name: Qasr Libya
desc: Site of Byzantine ruins famous for a Byzantine church containing fantastic floor mosaics.

name: Medina of Tripoli
desc: The walled historical heart of Tripoli, featuring traditional souks, old mosques, and narrow alleys.

name: Gharyan Troglodyte Caves
desc: Underground houses dug into the mountains, used for centuries for protection against extreme desert heat.

name: Zawiya of Al Jaghbub
desc: Former center of the Senussi order in the desert, an important historical and religious site.

name: Fort Capuzzo
desc: An Italian WWII fort on the border with Egypt, site of numerous military engagements.

name: Tobruk War Cemetery
desc: A memorial for Allied soldiers who fell during the Siege of Tobruk in World War II.

name: Knights of Malta Castle
desc: Remains of the short-lived fortifications of the Knights Hospitaller in Tripoli before the Ottoman conquest.

name: Murzuq Old Fort
desc: A ruin of a massive Ottoman fort in the Fezzan, once a key bastion for trans-Saharan caravans.

name: Awjila Old Mosque
desc: One of the oldest mosques in the Sahara, famous for its unusual conical domes.

name: Gurgi Mosque
desc: A beautifully decorated mosque in the heart of Tripoli, famous for its tile and marble work.

name: Karamanli Mosque
desc: An Ottoman mosque in Tripoli with fine stucco decorations, built by Ahmed Karamanli.

name: Al-Naga Mosque
desc: One of the oldest mosques in North Africa, rebuilt in 1610 following a fire.

name: Bir Hakeim Battlefield
desc: The site of a significant WWII battle where Free French forces heroically stood their ground.

name: Hospitaller Fort (Benghazi)
desc: Historical fort remains in Benghazi associated with the knightly orders and Ottoman rule.
